key_insight: A targeted pipeline that directly segments regions of interest (ROIs) for membranes in cryo-ET volumes and extracts morphological descriptors, enabling focused quantitative analysis without requiring full-structure segmentation.
problem_solved: Current cryo-ET workflows derive ROIs indirectly via complete structure segmentation, which is time-consuming, error-prone in noisy tomograms, and limits precise morphological quantification of membranes.
method: Direct ROI segmentation from tomograms using a learning-based model tailored to membrane appearance and contextual cues.
Automated morphological analysis computing per-ROI metrics (e.g., curvature, thickness, connectivity/topology) for quantitative characterization.
Integrated preprocessing and visualization steps (denoising/normalization, ROI filtering, 3D rendering) to support interpretation and downstream analysis.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to train and evaluate models on compact, biologically meaningful labels (ROIs) and to incorporate rich morphological features into downstream tasks (classification, phenotyping, generative modelling), improving efficiency and interpretability in cryo-ET analysis.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: tomogram → ROI segmentation → morphology extraction → visualization/metrics
Before/after tomogram slice with overlayed ROI masks to show targeted segmentation vs full segmentation
3D membrane rendering colored by morphological metrics (curvature, thickness) for intuitive spatial interpretation
Summary charts (box/violin plots or heatmaps) comparing key morphological descriptors across conditions or ROIs
paper_title: Region of Interest Segmentation and Morphological Analysis for Membranes in Cryo-Electron Tomography
paper_authors: Xingyi Cheng, Julien Maufront, Aurélie Di Cicco, Daniël M. Pelt, Manuela Dezi
